paras.en: CBS Evening News anchor Tony Dokoupil will moderate the event in Michigan, where elections for key seats in the Senate and House are taking place. Michigan voters, who also will be electing their first new governor in eight years, will be in attendance from across the political spectrum. They will be able to ask questions and share their thoughts.
paras.zh: 哥伦比亚广播公司晚间新闻主播托尼·多库皮尔将主持这场在密歇根州举行的活动，那里正在举行参议院和众议院关键席位的选举。密歇根州选民也将选举八年来的第一位新州长，来自各个政治派别的选民都将出席。他们将能够提出问题并分享他们的想法。

paras.en: According to CBS, issues discussed during the “Things That Matter” town hall will include the Congressional elections, affordability, tariffs, immigration, healthcare, artificial intelligence, the war with Iran and the state of our democracy.
paras.zh: 据哥伦比亚广播公司报道，“重要的事情”市政厅讨论的问题将包括国会选举、负担能力、关税、移民、医疗保健、人工智能、与伊朗的战争以及我们的民主状况。

paras.en: The one-hour special will air at 8 p.m. ET/PT on CBS and stream on Paramount+.
paras.zh: 一小时特别节目将于晚上 8 点播出。 ET/PT 在 CBS 上播出并在 Paramount+ 上播出。

paras.en: The special is a big push for Dokoupil, given the primetime timeslot and the big get with Vance. it also continues CBS editor-in-chief Bari Weiss’ desire to hold more town halls and buzzy events that include newsmakers.
paras.zh: 鉴于黄金时段和万斯的巨大收获，这部特别节目对多库皮尔来说是一个巨大的推动。它还延续了哥伦比亚广播公司 (CBS) 主编巴里·韦斯 (Bari Weiss) 的愿望，即举办更多包括新闻人物在内的市政厅和热闹活动。

paras.en: Previous CBS News town halls have featured the Artemis astronauts, former U.S. Sen. Ben Sasse (April 26) and Maryland Gov. Wes Moore.
paras.zh: 此前，CBS 新闻市政厅曾以阿耳忒弥斯号宇航员、前美国参议员本·萨斯 (Ben Sasse)（4 月 26 日）和马里兰州州长韦斯·摩尔 (Wes Moore) 为主角。

paras.en: Alexander Weprin contributed to this report.
paras.zh: 亚历山大·韦普林 (Alexander Weprin) 对本报告做出了贡献。

articles.title: Glen Powell Says He Doesn’t Want to Talk Politics, Blames Paramount Marketing Cuts for ‘The Running Man’ Box Office Performance
articles.author: McKinley Franklin

paras.en: Glen Powell isn’t interested in discussing politics.
paras.zh: 格伦·鲍威尔对讨论政治不感兴趣。

paras.en: In a new Esquire cover story, The Running Man actor said that despite his mother Cyndy Powell’s work in the U. S. Treasury Department under the Reagan administration, current events never made its way into his family’s dinner-table conversations. “Thank God,” he said.
paras.zh: 在《时尚先生》的新封面故事中，《奔跑吧兄弟》演员表示，尽管他的母亲辛迪·鲍威尔在里根政府时期的美国财政部工作，但时事从未进入他家人的餐桌谈话。 “感谢上帝，”他说。

paras.en: The actor said “over time” he has “realized that politics divide people. People trying to prove their point — for me, it’s the worst version of a conversation. I genuinely do not like the discourse. It’s not as healthy as it once was.”
paras.zh: 这位演员说，“随着时间的推移”，他“意识到政治分裂了人们。人们试图证明自己的观点——对我来说，这是最糟糕的对话版本。我真的不喜欢这种对话。它不像以前那么健康了。”

paras.en: Powell said that engaging in political conversations was “not presently possible.” He added, “I applaud people for jumping into those things and fighting for what they believe in. If I were a political person, I would be talking about it. For me, my calling is elsewhere.”
paras.zh: 鲍威尔表示，参与政治对话“目前不可能”。他补充道，“我赞扬人们投入这些事情并为他们的信仰而奋斗。如果我是一名政治人物，我会谈论它。对我来说，我的使命在别处。”

paras.en: The Top Gun: Maverick is not the only celebrity asserting their disinterest in speaking about politics. Powell’s Anyone But You co-star Sydney Sweeney said she has “never been here to talk about politics” in a cover interview with Cosmopolitan in January following the fallout from her viral American Eagle jeans ad.
paras.zh: 《壮志凌云：特立独行者》并不是唯一一个声称对谈论政治不感兴趣的名人。鲍威尔在《除你之外的任何人》中的联合主演西德尼·斯威尼 (Sydney Sweeney) 在 1 月份接受 Cosmopolitan 封面采访时表示，在她的 American Eagle 牛仔裤广告走红后，她“从来没有来这里谈论过政治”。

paras.en: Sweeney also said she doesn’t anticipate she will confirm her political beliefs: “I’m not a political person. I’m in the arts. I’m not here to speak on politics. That’s not an area I’ve ever even imagined getting into. It’s not why I became who I am. I became an actor because I like to tell stories, but I don’t believe in hate in any form. I believe we should all love each other and have respect and understanding for one another.”
paras.zh: 斯威尼还表示，她并不认为自己会证实自己的政治信仰：“我不是一个政治人物。我从事艺术工作。我不是来谈论政治的。这不是我曾经想象过的领域。这不是我成为现在的样子的原因。我成为一名演员是因为我喜欢讲故事，但我不相信任何形式的仇恨。我相信我们都应该彼此相爱，互相尊重和理解。”

paras.en: Last November, Jennifer Lawrence questioned if she should speak out against Trump after being vocal about her political stance during his first term.
paras.zh: 去年11月，詹妮弗·劳伦斯在特朗普第一个任期内直言不讳地表达了自己的政治立场后，质疑她是否应该公开反对特朗普。

paras.en: “I don’t really know if I should,” Lawrence told The New York Times on its The Interview podcast about speaking out against Trump and politics. “During the first Trump administration, I felt like I was running around like a chicken with my head cut off. But as we’ve learned, election after election, celebrities do not make a difference whatsoever on who people vote for. So then what am I doing? I’m just sharing my opinion on something that’s going to add fuel to a fire that’s ripping the country apart. We are so divided.”
paras.zh: “我真的不知道我是否应该这样做，”劳伦斯在《纽约时报》采访播客中谈到公开反对特朗普和政治时说道。 “在特朗普第一届政府期间，我感觉自己像一只被砍掉头的鸡一样到处乱跑。但正如我们所知，一次又一次的选举，名人对人们投票给谁没有任何影响。那么我在做什么呢？我只是在分享我的观点，这会火上浇油，导致国家分裂。我们的分歧很大。”

paras.en: Elsewhere in the profile, Powell addressed The Running Man‘s weak box office performance. “They let go of an entire marketing department a month before our movie came out in the middle of a merger,” he said of Paramount, the studio behind the film.
paras.zh: 在简介的其他地方，鲍威尔谈到了《奔跑吧兄弟》票房表现不佳的问题。 “在我们的电影上映前一个月，他们在合并过程中解雇了整个营销部门，”他谈到电影背后的派拉蒙工作室时说道。

paras.en: The Running Man released on Nov. 14, 2025; on Oct. 29, The Hollywood Reporter reported that Paramount began series of staff cuts, resulting in about 1,000 jobs being impacted.
paras.zh: 《跑男》于 2025 年 11 月 14 日上映； 10月29日，《好莱坞报道》报道称，派拉蒙开始进行一系列裁员，导致约1000个工作岗位受到影响。

paras.en: THR reached out to Paramount for comment, but did not hear back by the time of publication.
paras.zh: 《好莱坞报道》联系派拉蒙请其置评，但截至发稿时尚未收到回复。

articles.title: Supertanker chartered from Gulf Coast to China for $76 million, 10 times higher than pre-war level

paras.en: A supertanker was recently chartered to sail from the U.S. Gulf Coast to China for $76 million, a source familiar told CNBC, as shipping costs soar globally due to the crisis in the Middle East.
paras.zh: 一位知情人士向 CNBC 透露，由于中东危机导致全球航运成本飙升，最近一艘超级油轮以 7600 万美元的价格租用，从美国墨西哥湾沿岸驶往中国。

paras.en: The Alexandros was chartered by the trading firm Trafigura and is expected to load around Nov. 19, the source said. A normal rate for the route based on pre-war levels would be $7 million to $10 million.
paras.zh: 消息人士称，“Alexandros”号由贸易公司托克 (Trafigura) 租用，预计将于 11 月 19 日左右装船。根据战前水平，该路线的正常费率为 700 万至 1000 万美元。

paras.en: The cost of the journey comes to $38 per barrel of oil assuming the tanker holds 2 million barrels. Shipping costs have exploded as the war in the Persian Gulf has led to a shortage of available tankers.
paras.zh: 假设油轮载有 200 万桶石油，这一旅程的成本为每桶石油 38 美元。由于波斯湾战争导致可用油轮短缺，运输成本激增。

paras.en: The Middle East producers are using a shuttle system to export oil through the Strait of Hormuz. A loaded tanker crosses the strait and then loads the oil onto another ship in the Gulf of Oman that takes the cargo to Asia.
paras.zh: 中东生产商正在使用航天飞机系统通过霍尔木兹海峡出口石油。一艘满载的油轮穿过海峡，然后将石油装载到阿曼湾的另一艘船上，将货物运往亚洲。

paras.en: This system reduces the exposure to Iranian attack and has led to a rebound of crude exports through Hormuz. But it also requires a lot more ships to get the oil out of the Gulf.
paras.zh: 该系统减少了遭受伊朗袭击的风险，并导致霍尔木兹原油出口反弹。但也需要更多的船只将石油运出海湾。

articles.title: Microsoft to sell $2,599 Surface Laptop Ultra containing Nvidia AI chip

paras.en: Microsoft said its new laptop containing an Nvidia AI chip will start at $2,599, as the software maker tries to bring more artificial intelligence capabilities to its consumer devices.
paras.zh: 微软表示，其搭载 Nvidia AI 芯片的新款笔记本电脑起价为 2,599 美元，该软件制造商试图为其消费设备带来更多人工智能功能。

paras.en: The Surface Laptop Ultra is now available on preorder and will begin shipping on Oct. 16, Pavan Davuluri, Microsoft's executive vice president of Windows and devices, said at a company event in San Francisco on Wednesday. The computer has the world's first magnetic USB-C port, similar to Apple's MagSafe charging connector, along with two other standard USB-C ports, Microsoft said in a blog post.
paras.zh: 微软 Windows 和设备执行副总裁 Pavan Davuluri 周三在旧金山举行的一次公司活动上表示，Surface Laptop Ultra 现已开始接受预订，并将于 10 月 16 日开始发货。微软在博客文章中表示，该电脑拥有世界上第一个磁性 USB-C 端口，类似于苹果的 MagSafe 充电连接器，以及另外两个标准 USB-C 端口。

paras.en: While Microsoft Windows is the most popular operating system for PCs, the company isn't among the top six PC vendors in terms of unit shipments, according to an estimate from researcher Gartner. As the AI boom matures and chip technology advances, tech giants including Microsoft, Apple and Google are aiming to allow users to run more AI workloads from their devices rather than relying on the cloud.
paras.zh: 根据研究机构 Gartner 的估计，虽然 Microsoft Windows 是最流行的 PC 操作系统，但就出货量而言，该公司并未跻身前六名 PC 供应商之列。随着人工智能热潮的成熟和芯片技术的进步，微软、苹果和谷歌等科技巨头的目标是让用户从他们的设备上运行更多的人工智能工作负载，而不是依赖云。

paras.en: Users can install and run a variety of models on the new laptop without having to worry about racking up high monthly bills. Microsoft first talked about the Surface Laptop Ultra in May, but is just now providing specifics.
paras.zh: 用户可以在新笔记本电脑上安装和运行各种型号，而不必担心每月收取高额账单。微软于 5 月份首次谈论 Surface Laptop Ultra，但现在才提供具体细节。

paras.en: "Microsoft might get me back to Windows," Max Weinbach, an analyst at Creative Strategies, wrote on X after the announcement.
paras.zh: Creative Strategies 分析师马克斯·温巴赫 (Max Weinbach) 在宣布这一消息后在 X 上写道：“微软可能会让我回到 Windows。”

paras.en: Davuluri also said that Meta will introduce a version of its popular Muse AI agent for Windows, capitalizing on the surging popularity of the personal agent, which has jumped to the top of Apple's App store, surpassing ChatGPT.
paras.zh: Davuluri 还表示，Meta 将推出其流行的 Windows 版 Muse AI 代理，利用个人代理的高涨人气，该代理已跃居苹果应用商店榜首，超越 ChatGPT。

paras.en: Microsoft is still trying to solidify its role as a key player in AI. The company offers its own AI models, but they're less popular than leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic and aren't at the forefront in terms of performance, according to one benchmark. Developers are more likely to have used alternatives, according to a recent survey.
paras.zh: 微软仍在努力巩固其作为人工智能领域关键参与者的角色。该公司提供自己的人工智能模型，但根据一项基准测试，它们不如 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的领先模型受欢迎，而且在性能方面并不处于领先地位。根据最近的一项调查，开发商更有可能使用替代方案。

paras.en: This isn't the first time Microsoft has sought to use the AI boom as a way to boost sales of its devices.
paras.zh: 这并不是微软第一次寻求利用人工智能热潮来提高其设备的销量。

paras.en: In 2024, the company introduced the Copilot+ PC standard, requiring the inclusion of neural processing units that ensure a minimum level of AI performance, along with compliant Surface computers. But Microsoft has since "simplified product naming to lead with the Surface brand, while continuing to deliver premium hardware and hybrid AI experiences," a spokesperson said.
paras.zh: 2024 年，该公司推出了 Copilot+ PC 标准，要求包含可确保最低水平 AI 性能的神经处理单元以及兼容的 Surface 计算机。但微软发言人表示，自此之后，微软“简化了产品命名，以 Surface 品牌为主导，同时继续提供优质硬件和混合人工智能体验”。

paras.en: The new device can contain up to 128 gigabytes of unified memory and supply up to one petaflop of computing power. The Blackwell RTX Spark GPU inside the computer has as much processing power as Nvidia's DGX-1 data center server from 2016, which cost $250 million, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said at Wednesday's event.
paras.zh: 新设备可包含高达 128 GB 的统一内存，并提供高达 1 petaflop 的计算能力。 Nvidia 首席执行官 Jensen Huang 在周三的活动中表示，计算机内的 Blackwell RTX Spark GPU 的处理能力与 Nvidia 2016 年的 DGX-1 数据中心服务器相当，后者耗资 2.5 亿美元。

paras.en: A presenter showed how apps on the Surface Laptop Ultra can route some AI coding requests run on the computer's local GPU, displaying a green leaf icon, and others to the cloud. Through Windows 11, developers can confine coding agents to Microsoft Execution Containers that will prevent unwanted system access.
paras.zh: 演示者展示了 Surface Laptop Ultra 上的应用程序如何将在计算机本地 GPU 上运行的一些 AI 编码请求（显示绿叶图标）和其他请求路由到云端。通过 Windows 11，开发人员可以将编码代理限制在 Microsoft 执行容器中，以防止不必要的系统访问。

paras.en: Microsoft is updating its Windows 11 device setup experience to help people get started quickly with open-source OpenClaw AI agent software.
paras.zh: Microsoft 正在更新其 Windows 11 设备设置体验，以帮助人们快速开始使用开源 OpenClaw AI 代理软件。

paras.en: Microsoft has been releasing its own computers since 2012, and CEO Satya Nadella indicated on Tuesday that the company's position in the market is evolving.
paras.zh: 微软自 2012 年以来一直在发布自己的电脑，首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 周二表示，该公司在市场上的地位正在演变。

paras.en: "I think today is the day we'll start talking and thinking about the frontier ecosystem taking maybe slightly different contours two years from now, five years from now, 10 years from now," Nadella said at the event. "That classic edge that distributed computing will always remain distributed will be more true."
paras.zh: 纳德拉在活动中表示：“我认为今天是我们开始讨论和思考前沿生态系统的一天，两年后、五年后、十年后，前沿生态系统的轮廓可能会略有不同。” “分布式计算将始终保持分布式这一经典优势将更加真实。”

articles.title: Trump’s diesel order exposes White House limits to counter surging fuel prices

paras.en: Truckers likely won't see much in the way of relief from President Donald Trump's executive order that allows them to use off-road diesel fuel on America's highways without federal penalties, analysts say.
paras.zh: 分析人士表示，唐纳德·特朗普总统的行政命令允许卡车司机在美国高速公路上使用越野柴油而不受联邦处罚，卡车司机可能不会看到太大的缓解。

paras.en: Off-road diesel is exempt from federal and state excise taxes because it is used for construction and farm equipment, railways and to heat homes. It is dyed red to differentiate it from taxed on-road diesel, but is otherwise the same fuel.
paras.zh: 非公路柴油可免征联邦和州消费税，因为它用于建筑和农用设备、铁路以及家庭供暖。它被染成红色，以区别于征税的道路柴油，但在其他方面是相同的燃料。

paras.en: The federal government charges an excise tax of 24.4 cents per gallon for on-road diesel. In theory, Trump's order spares truckers the tax by allowing them to use red-dyed fuel on the highway, without worrying that the federal government will impose penalties.
paras.zh: 联邦政府对道路柴油征收每加仑 24.4 美分的消费税。从理论上讲，特朗普的命令允许卡车司机在高速公路上使用红色燃料，从而免除了他们的税收，而不必担心联邦政府会施加处罚。

paras.en: But the president's action only defers the actual tax payment itself until the end of the year, while calling on the Treasury Secretary to look for ways to eliminate the deferred obligation altogether.
paras.zh: 但总统的行动只是将实际纳税本身推迟到年底，同时呼吁财政部长寻找完全消除递延义务的方法。

paras.en: "While it might be deferred, it may not disappear entirely," said Andy Lipow, president of Lipow Oil Associates. "Maybe you save a little bit of money up front, but you might have to pay it to the government later."
paras.zh: Lipow Oil Associates 总裁安迪·利波 (Andy Lipow) 表示：“虽然它可能会被推迟，但它可能不会完全消失。” “也许你可以先存一点钱，但以后可能需要向政府支付。”

paras.en: Trump cannot defer state excise taxes, which can be higher than the federal obligation, at a national average of 35.5 cents per gallon. Some states have taken independent action to give relief to diesel users.
paras.zh: 特朗普不能推迟州消费税，该税可能高于联邦义务，全国平均税率为每加仑 35.5 美分。一些州已采取独立行动，为柴油用户提供救济。

paras.en: Although Trump is waiving federal penalties for using off-road diesel on highways, states in principle could enforce their local laws prohibiting the red-dyed fuel on the road.
paras.zh: 尽管特朗普免除了对在高速公路上使用越野柴油的联邦处罚，但各州原则上可以执行当地法律，禁止在道路上使用红色燃料。

paras.en: "It's not like every state trooper is going to pull over the truck and look at your diesel fuel, but you're a trucker — do you need that aggravation?" Lipow said.
paras.zh: “并不是每个州警都会把卡车停下来检查你的柴油，但你是一名卡车司机——你需要这么恼怒吗？”利波说道。

paras.en: Trump's executive order comes as he faces political pressure to take action on diesel prices ahead of midterm elections on Nov. 3, when Republicans face competitive races in farm states such as Iowa. Retail diesel prices hit a record high in September and currently average $6.30 a gallon nationally, according to AAA.
paras.zh: 特朗普发布行政命令之际，他面临着在 11 月 3 日中期选举之前对柴油价格采取行动的政治压力，届时共和党将在爱荷华州等农业州面临激烈的竞选。根据 AAA 的数据，9 月份柴油零售价格创下历史新高，目前全国平均柴油价格为每加仑 6.30 美元。

paras.en: The president flirted with a diesel export ban last month but ultimately abandoned the idea, telling reporters Friday that "it was never really on the table." The oil industry and big business groups were staunchly opposed. Trump publicly voiced concerns that a diesel export ban would raise gasoline prices.
paras.zh: 总统上个月曾考虑实施柴油出口禁令，但最终放弃了这个想法，周五告诉记者“它从未真正提上台面”。石油工业和大企业集团坚决反对。特朗普公开表达了对柴油出口禁令将提高汽油价格的担忧。

paras.en: Diesel futures dropped overnight Monday into Tuesday morning after Trump's executive order, but ultimately turned higher. Futures were up more than 1% Wednesday.
paras.zh: 在特朗普发布行政命令后，柴油期货周一至周二上午隔夜下跌，但最终走高。周三期货上涨超过 1%。

paras.en: "What it shows you is there are no good options for the administration or any administration to bring down the price of fuel, because the bottleneck is refineries," Lipow said.
paras.zh: “这表明政府或任何政府都没有好的选择来降低燃料价格，因为瓶颈在于炼油厂，”利波说。

paras.en: Diesel prices are high around the world because Ukraine is bombarding Russian refineries and strikes by Iran and its allies have taken capacity offline in the Middle East.
paras.zh: 由于乌克兰轰炸俄罗斯炼油厂，以及伊朗及其盟国的罢工导致中东产能停产，全球柴油价格居高不下。

paras.en: G7 countries led by France, facing pressure from the Trump administration, agreed Friday to release diesel stocks, though it's unclear in what quantities.
paras.zh: 以法国为首的七国集团国家面临特朗普政府的压力，周五同意释放柴油库存，但具体数量尚不清楚。

paras.en: "They're pulling every every lever they can," Jeff Currie, CEO of Real Macro and a senior advisor at Carlyle, told CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Tuesday.
paras.zh: Real Macro 首席执行官兼凯雷高级顾问杰夫·柯里 (Jeff Currie) 周二对 CNBC 的“Squawk Box”节目表示：“他们正在竭尽全力。”

paras.en: But Trump's executive order allowing red-dyed diesel on the road "won't have a profound impact" on fuel prices, Currie said.
paras.zh: 但柯里表示，特朗普允许红色柴油上路的行政命令“不会对燃油价格产生深远影响”。

paras.en: There is one action the administration could take that would be effective, Lipow said. "End the conflict."
paras.zh: 利波说，政府可以采取一项有效的行动。 “结束冲突。”

paras.en: "The Strait [of Hormuz] reopens, oil flows, those refineries in the Middle East start kicking up runs, more refined products make it to the market," the analyst said. "The market will react to that."
paras.zh: 这位分析师表示：“霍尔木兹海峡重新开放，石油流动，中东的炼油厂开始开工，更多的精炼产品进入市场。” “市场将会对此做出反应。”

articles.title: What is AI model distillation, and why is it so hard to stop?

paras.en: To make grain-based liquor, you heat a fermented mash in a still until alcohol-rich vapor rises and then cool it back into a stronger liquid. Chemists and whiskey makers know this as distillation. Artificial intelligence developers have borrowed the word to describe boiling down a big AI model into a smaller one—and lately the biggest AI companies say that rivals have been distilling like bootleggers.
paras.zh: 为了酿造谷物酒，您需要在蒸馏器中加热发酵的麦芽浆，直到富含酒精的蒸气上升，然后将其冷却回更浓的液体。化学家和威士忌制造商将其称为蒸馏。人工智能开发人员借用这个词来形容将大型人工智能模型精简为较小的模型——最近，最大的人工智能公司表示，竞争对手一直在像盗版者一样进行提炼。

paras.en: In September Anthropic and OpenAI each detailed how they caught and killed campaigns to distill their flagship models—that is, to extract enough information from the models to train new models that mimic the originals at a fraction of the size and cost.
paras.zh: 9 月，Anthropic 和 OpenAI 各自详细介绍了他们如何抓住并扼杀提炼其旗舰模型的活动，即从模型中提取足够的信息来训练模仿原始模型的新模型，而其规模和成本却只有一小部分。

paras.en: Distillation has become a sore spot for American AI companies as they try to justify high valuations and fight off competition from each other and open-source alternatives. If, say, a Chinese model developer can piggyback on all the money and computing power those companies have invested, the incentive to keep making new models starts to evaporate.
paras.zh: 蒸馏已成为美国人工智能公司的痛处，因为它们试图证明高估值的合理性，并对抗彼此和开源替代品的竞争。比如说，如果中国模型开发商能够利用这些公司投资的所有资金和计算能力，那么继续制作新模型的动力就会开始消失。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: And no one expects distillation to stop any time soon—so we asked the researchers who study it to explain the situation.
paras.zh: 没有人预计蒸馏会很快停止，因此我们请研究它的研究人员解释这一情况。

paras.en: Just as a still concentrates a large batch of weak liquid into a smaller batch of strong stuff, AI distillation condenses a big model into a smaller one that, ideally, acts like the original. The process starts with the existing large model, called the teacher. Developers prompt the teacher many times over and then feed its responses into the new model, called the student, to train the latter.
paras.zh: 就像蒸馏器将大量稀液体浓缩成一小批浓液体一样，人工智能蒸馏将一个大模型浓缩成一个较小的模型，理想情况下，它的作用与原始模型一样。该过程从现有的大型模型（称为教师）开始。开发人员多次提示老师，然后将其响应输入到称为学生的新模型中，以训练后者。

paras.en: In a way, every response contains information about what the teacher learned during training, so that knowledge passes to the student without going through the process of collecting data, finding patterns in those data and getting human feedback. Distillation lets someone reverse engineer an AI model just by using it and watching its responses.
paras.zh: 在某种程度上，每个响应都包含有关教师在培训期间学到的内容的信息，因此知识可以传递给学生，而无需经历收集数据、查找这些数据中的模式和获取人类反馈的过程。蒸馏让人们只需使用它并观察其响应即可对人工智能模型进行逆向工程。

paras.en: It helps that AI models tend to give away more than just their final answers. “Oftentimes the teacher model doesn’t just give you the label, but it actually gives you more fine-grained information,” says Yevgeniy Vorobeychik, a professor of computer science at Washington University in St. Louis. That could include the odds a model assigns to each possible response or, as in the case OpenAI described, an encrypted record of the step-by-step reasoning its more powerful models work through before they answer.
paras.zh: 人工智能模型往往会给出的不仅仅是最终答案，这一点很有帮助。圣路易斯华盛顿大学计算机科学教授叶夫根尼·沃罗贝奇克 (Yevgeniy Vorobeychik) 表示：“教师模型通常不仅仅为您提供标签，而且实际上为您提供更细粒度的信息。”这可能包括模型分配给每个可能响应的几率，或者如 OpenAI 所描述的情况那样，包括其更强大的模型在回答之前逐步推理的加密记录。

paras.en: Plenty of distillation is aboveboard. Smaller models let developers get more for less. In fact, the concept predates large language models (LLMs); by the 2000s, researchers were studying it as a way to increase efficiency for neural networks. “We cared about making it smaller, easier to use, faster to apply,” says Alexandru Niculescu-Mizil, a machine learning researcher at Qube Research & Technologies, who cowrote an early paper on the idea in 2006.
paras.zh: 大量的蒸馏是光明正大的。较小的模型可以让开发人员以更少的成本获得更多的成果。事实上，这个概念早于大型语言模型（LLM）。到了 2000 年代，研究人员开始研究它作为提高神经网络效率的一种方法。 Qube Research & Technologies 的机器学习研究员 Alexandru Niculescu-Mizil 表示：“我们希望使其更小、更易于使用、应用更快。”他于 2006 年与他人共同撰写了一篇关于这一想法的早期论文。

paras.en: Distilling someone else’s model is another matter. The term first caught mainstream attention in early 2025, when DeepSeek, then a little-known Chinese start-up, released a reasoning model, called R1, that it said it had trained for less than $300,000—a fraction of what American labs had spent. Allegations quickly emerged that DeepSeek had trained R1 in part on responses extracted from OpenAI’s models.
paras.zh: 提炼别人的模型是另一回事。这个术语首次引起主流关注是在 2025 年初，当时一家名不见经传的中国初创公司 DeepSeek 发布了一款名为 R1 的推理模型，据称该模型的训练成本不到 30 万美元——只是美国实验室花费的一小部分。很快就有指控称 DeepSeek 部分地根据从 OpenAI 模型中提取的响应来训练 R1。

paras.en: These days the word is generally associated with accusations of model theft, mostly aimed at Chinese developers such as DeepSeek and Moonshot AI, the maker of Kimi. In their September reports, Anthropic and OpenAI both blamed labs based in China for the recent distillation campaigns they caught, calling the activity “illicit” and “unauthorized.” DeepSeek and Moonshot AI have both fended off these accusations in the past. Of course, Anthropic and OpenAI have themselves been accused of training their models on data obtained without authorization from all over the internet.
paras.zh: 如今，这个词通常与模型盗窃的指控联系在一起，主要针对 DeepSeek 和 Kimi 的制造商 Moonshot AI 等中国开发商。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 在 9 月份的报告中都将最近发现的蒸馏活动归咎于中国实验室，称该活动“非法”且“未经授权”。 DeepSeek 和 Moonshot AI 过去都曾驳斥过这些指控。当然，Anthropic 和 OpenAI 本身也被指控利用未经授权从互联网上获得的数据来训练他们的模型。

paras.en: Still, though the companies also cast distillation as a security risk, their most obvious interest in stopping it is protecting their competitive advantage. “The text that it produces in response to your prompt is being stolen by some rival companies,” says Alexander Panfilov, a Ph.D. student at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems in Germany. “But on a conceptual level, what you are stealing [are] capabilities.”
paras.zh: 尽管如此，尽管这些公司也将蒸馏视为一种安全风险，但他们阻止蒸馏的最明显利益是保护自己的竞争优势。 “它根据你的提示生成的文本正在被一些竞争对手公司窃取，”博士亚历山大·潘菲洛夫 (Alexander Panfilov) 说。德国马克斯·普朗克智能系统研究所的学生。 “但在概念层面上，你窃取的是能力。”

paras.en: In general, distillation is done by collecting thousands and thousands of AI responses to different kinds of queries. Those prompts and responses then become training data for the student, usually through a process called supervised fine-tuning, which treats the teacher’s answers as targets the student should try to emulate. Over many rounds, training nudges the student’s internal settings, called weights, so that its answers more closely match the teacher’s.
paras.zh: 一般来说，蒸馏是通过收集成千上万的人工智能对不同类型查询的响应来完成的。这些提示和响应通常会通过一个称为监督微调的过程成为学生的训练数据，该过程将教师的答案视为学生应该尝试模仿的目标。在多轮训练中，训练会推动学生的内部设置（称为权重），使其答案更接近老师的答案。

paras.en: The key is getting those data. Anthropic and OpenAI have detailed several creative methods they believe attackers used to do so. According to Anthropic, some labs routed their own customers’ prompts to Claude and then saved Claude’s responses to train their own models. The company also said that distillers try to obscure where they are located. OpenAI, meanwhile, said distillers tried to get at its models’ hidden reasoning by “copying encrypted reasoning from one conversation and asking a model in another conversation to decrypt” it.
paras.zh: 关键是获取这些数据。 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 详细介绍了他们认为攻击者常用的几种创造性方法。据 Anthropic 称，一些实验室将自己客户的提示发送给克劳德，然后保存克劳德的回答来训练自己的模型。该公司还表示，酿酒厂试图掩盖其所在地。与此同时，OpenAI 表示，蒸馏器试图通过“复制一个对话中的加密推理并要求另一个对话中的模型解密”来了解其模型的隐藏推理。

paras.en: Panfilov was co-lead author of a preprint paper detailing that kind of attack, and OpenAI credited him and his colleagues with bringing the attacks to the company’s attention. In this case, the goal was to distill how the models reason, or generate longer responses in order to solve hard problems step-by-step. Panfilov and his colleagues called their project “Stolen Thoughts,” a sign of how tightly the concept has become intertwined with thievery.
paras.zh: 潘菲洛夫是一篇预印本论文的共同主要作者，该论文详细介绍了此类攻击，OpenAI 称赞他和他的同事让公司注意到了这些攻击。在这种情况下，目标是提炼模型的推理方式，或生成更长的响应，以便逐步解决难题。潘菲洛夫和他的同事将他们的项目称为“被盗的想法”，这表明这个概念与盗窃紧密地交织在一起。

paras.en: The AI companies are hesitant to reveal exactly how they caught these latest attempts because doing so would show the next distiller what to avoid. Broadly, though, the firms seem to have watched for accounts prompting their models in suspicious ways, whether by firing off lots of prompts in a short time or by asking telltale kinds of questions. Anthropic, for instance, said that, from May to July, it observed more than 151 million exchanges between Claude and accounts tied to Chinese e-commerce giant Alibaba, which also makes the Qwen family of AI models.
paras.zh: 人工智能公司不愿透露他们是如何捕捉到这些最新尝试的，因为这样做会告诉下一个蒸馏器应该避免什么。不过，总体而言，这些公司似乎一直在关注以可疑方式提示其模型的账户，无论是在短时间内发出大量提示，还是提出泄露信息的问题。例如，Anthropic 表示，从 5 月到 7 月，它观察到 Claude 与中国电子商务巨头阿里巴巴相关账户之间的交易次数超过 1.51 亿次，阿里巴巴也生产 Qwen 系列人工智能模型。

paras.en: Panfilov says the attack he studied is easy to detect, but he worries that cleverer ones can’t be spotted without trampling everyone’s privacy. “I don’t have a good idea how [AI companies] would do it, especially given that they claim this zero data retention policy,” he says, referring to arrangements under which the companies don’t store some customers’ prompts and responses.
paras.zh: 潘菲洛夫表示，他研究的攻击很容易被发现，但他担心，如果不侵犯每个人的隐私，就无法发现更聪明的攻击。他说：“我不太清楚（人工智能公司）会如何做到这一点，特别是考虑到他们声称实行零数据保留政策。”他指的是这些公司不存储某些客户的提示和回复的安排。

paras.en: Both OpenAI and Anthropic have warned that the distillers’ methods will only get more sophisticated, given how valuable distillation can be.
paras.zh: OpenAI 和 Anthropic 都警告说，考虑到蒸馏的价值，蒸馏器的方法只会变得更加复杂。

paras.en: The trouble is that the very qualities that make AI models informative and useful also make them good to train on. So attempts to make a model harder to distill may also make it worse. Over the summer, Vorobeychik and his colleagues found that a model’s reasoning can be rewritten so that it will make poor training material for a copycat, without making the model’s answers any less accurate. They also found that the rewritten reasoning was harder for people to follow, however. “Just by virtue of the fact that they’re harder to read for the LLM to train, it’s also harder for humans to digest,” Vorobeychik says. That’s an unwelcome trade for a technology whose output already takes flak for being hard to parse.
paras.zh: 问题在于，人工智能模型具有信息丰富性和实用性的特质也使得它们很适合训练。因此，尝试让模型更难提炼也可能会让情况变得更糟。今年夏天，沃罗贝奇克和他的同事发现模型的推理可以被重写，这样它就可以成为模仿者的糟糕培训材料，同时又不会降低模型答案的准确性。然而，他们还发现，重写后的推理更难让人理解。 “由于它们更难阅读以供法学硕士培训，因此人类也更难消化，”沃罗贝奇克说。对于一项技术来说，这是一项不受欢迎的交易，因为该技术的输出已经因难以解析而受到批评。

paras.en: Panfilov also notes that distillation can be done in pieces in which “each query in itself is benign.” That would make it even harder to distinguish someone prompting a model for ordinary use from someone trying to build a model of their own. AI companies will have to balance protecting their models’ capabilities against actually flexing them for the public, which is, after all, what they’re selling.
paras.zh: 潘菲洛夫还指出，蒸馏可以分块进行，其中“每个查询本身都是良性的”。这将使区分促使模型用于普通用途的人和试图构建自己的模型的人变得更加困难。人工智能公司必须在保护其模型的功能与实际向公众展示它们之间取得平衡，毕竟，这才是他们所销售的。

paras.en: All this suggests that stopping illicit distillation will mean finding new attacks before stamping them out. The labs, in effect, are playing revenuers, the liquor-tax agents who once hunted down and dismantled illegal stills. But as fears about distillation intertwine with fears about Chinese AI capabilities more broadly, busting stills one at a time may not be enough to put the American AI industry at ease.
paras.zh: 所有这些都表明，停止非法蒸馏将意味着在消灭新的攻击之前发现它们。事实上，这些实验室正在扮演收税者的角色，他们是曾经追捕并拆除非法蒸馏器的酒类税代理人。但随着对蒸馏的担忧与对中国人工智能能力的更广泛担忧交织在一起，一次破坏一张静态图片可能不足以让美国人工智能行业放心。

articles.title: Why does weed cause anxiety? A new brain study investigates cannabis paranoia

paras.en: Whether you are smoking or eating it, marijuana can be relaxing—or it can cause feelings of anxiety, panic and paranoia. But despite the prevalence of these unnerving experiences—studies suggest frequent cannabis use is associated with higher odds of anxiety—scientists have little understanding as to why they occur.
paras.zh: 无论您是吸食还是吸食大麻，大麻都可以让人放松，但也可能引起焦虑、恐慌和偏执的感觉。尽管这些令人不安的经历很普遍——研究表明频繁吸食大麻与更高的焦虑几率有关——但科学家们对它们发生的原因知之甚少。

paras.en: “From a biological perspective, we really know almost nothing,” says Sachin Patel, a neuroscientist at Northwestern University.
paras.zh: “从生物学的角度来看，我们实际上几乎一无所知，”西北大学的神经科学家萨钦·帕特尔说。

paras.en: In a bid to understand why one of the world’s most popular drugs summons such negative emotions, Patel and his colleagues investigated its effect on mice. The team’s findings, published last week in Nature Communications, reveal that, when given such a drug, rodents suffer adverse reactions similar to the paranoia human cannabis users feel. The effect is driven by a specific group of neurons in the central amygdala, a brain region that processes fear and anxiety.
paras.zh: 为了了解为什么世界上最受欢迎的药物之一会引起如此负面的情绪，帕特尔和他的同事研究了它对老鼠的影响。该研究小组上周发表在《自然通讯》上的研究结果表明，当给予这种药物时，啮齿类动物会出现类似于人类大麻使用者偏执的不良反应。这种效应是由杏仁核中央的一组特定神经元驱动的，杏仁核是处理恐惧和焦虑的大脑区域。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The researchers injected mice with varying doses of CP55940, a synthetic cannabinoid that mimics the effects of tetrahydrocannabinol, or TCH, the main psychoactive compound in weed. Then they placed the mice in a cage with a petri dish full of fox urine. As expected, the animals became anxious, either fleeing the threatening odor or freezing in place. These responses were more extreme in mice who received larger doses—a relatable result if you’ve ever found yourself peering suspiciously through the living room blinds after one toke too many.
paras.zh: 研究人员给小鼠注射了不同剂量的 CP55940，这是一种合成大麻素，可以模仿四氢大麻酚（TCH）的作用，TCH 是杂草中主要的精神活性化合物。然后他们将小鼠放入装有装满狐狸尿液的培养皿的笼子中。正如预期的那样，动物们变得焦虑起来，要么逃离威胁性的气味，要么僵在原地。这些反应在接受较大剂量的老鼠中更为极端——如果你发现自己在服用过多的老鼠后，发现自己透过客厅的百叶窗怀疑地凝视着，那么这个结果是相关的。

paras.en: To tease out a connection between the animals’ behavior and their brain activity, the researchers turned to the central amygdala, which past research has shown to play a role in threat responses. Looking through small microscopes implanted in the mice’s heads, Patel’s team zoomed in on a particular subset of brain cells, called somatostatin neurons, as the animals reacted to the fox urine scent. “The take-home,” Patel says, “was that those cells were hyperactive when combining cannabinoids with the stress exposure.”
paras.zh: 为了弄清楚动物的行为和大脑活动之间的联系，研究人员转向中央杏仁核，过去的研究表明杏仁核在威胁反应中发挥着作用。通过植入小鼠头部的小型显微镜，帕特尔的团队放大了一个特定的脑细胞子集，称为生长抑素神经元，当动物对狐狸尿液的气味做出反应时。 “结果是，”帕特尔说，“当大麻素与压力暴露相结合时，这些细胞会变得过度活跃。”

paras.en: The researchers found that cannabinoids suppress the release of a neurotransmitter called gamma-aminobutyric acid, or GABA, which tamps down brain activity. In other words, the drug essentially weakens the central amygdala’s “brake,” Patel says, allowing fear and anxiety to run wild. When the researchers silenced the somatostatin neurons, the mice stopped trying so hard to avoid the threatening odor in their midst.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，大麻素会抑制一种名为γ-氨基丁酸（GABA）的神经递质的释放，这种神经递质会抑制大脑活动。换句话说，这种药物本质上削弱了中央杏仁核的“刹车”，帕特尔说，让恐惧和焦虑失控。当研究人员使生长抑素神经元沉默后，小鼠就不再那么努力地躲避它们中间的威胁性气味。

paras.en: “This elegantly demonstrates a causal role,” says Ozge Gunduz-Cinar, a neuroscientist at the U.S. National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism, who was not involved in the study. She notes, however, that the researchers “examined only a single inhibitory cell type in a single brain region using an innate fear model,” suggesting there may be more to this story.
paras.zh: “这巧妙地证明了因果关系，”美国国家酒精滥用和酒精中毒研究所的神经科学家奥兹格·冈杜兹-西纳尔（Ozge Gunduz-Cinar）说，他没有参与这项研究。然而，她指出，研究人员“使用先天恐惧模型仅检查了单个大脑区域中的单一抑制细胞类型”，这表明这个故事可能还有更多内容。

paras.en: Humans are not mice, so it is unclear whether our own cannabis-induced anxiety arises in the exact same way. But Patel suspects a similar mechanism, given that stoned mice exhibit a pattern of behavior that might feel familiar to anyone who’s overdone it on edibles. “The fact that we can mimic that behavioral response in animals quite nicely makes me think that the neural data we have has some relevance to what’s probably going on in humans,” he says.
paras.zh: 人类不是老鼠，因此尚不清楚我们自己的大麻引起的焦虑是否以完全相同的方式产生。但帕特尔怀疑存在类似的机制，因为中毒的老鼠表现出的一种行为模式可能会让那些吃太多食物的人感到熟悉。 “我们可以很好地模仿动物的行为反应，这一事实让我认为我们拥有的神经数据与人类可能发生的事情有一定的相关性，”他说。

paras.en: Human relevance might be difficult to prove, though. You could hypothetically get someone high, put them in a brain scanner, make them stare at pictures of scary faces and then look to see how their brain activity changes as dread wells up inside them—but that wouldn’t be very kind. “It’s a little difficult from an ethical perspective,” Patel acknowledges. Still, he believes that a deeper understanding of how marijuana affects the brain could produce new ways to counteract a bad trip.
paras.zh: 不过，人类的相关性可能很难证明。假设你可以让某人兴奋起来，将他们放入脑部扫描仪中，让他们盯着恐怖面孔的照片，然后看看当恐惧在他们内心涌动时，他们的大脑活动如何变化——但这并不是很好。 “从道德角度来看，这有点困难，”帕特尔承认。尽管如此，他相信，更深入地了解大麻如何影响大脑可能会产生新的方法来抵消糟糕的旅行。

articles.title: The Atlantic hurricane season has been eerily quiet—Tropical Storm Isaias could change that

paras.en: Tropical Storm Isaias, a cyclone in the Gulf of Mexico, is expected to strengthen into a hurricane by Thursday, according to the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. If it does, Isaias would be the latest-forming first hurricane in the Atlantic season since reliable records began.
paras.zh: 据美国国家海洋和大气管理局称，墨西哥湾的热带气旋伊萨亚斯预计将在周四增强为飓风。如果确实如此，伊萨亚斯将成为自有可靠记录以来大西洋季节中最新形成的第一场飓风。

paras.en: As of Wednesday morning, Isaias sat about 260 miles (420 kilometers) off the coast of Progreso, Mexico, and NOAA forecast that it is headed toward the U.S. Gulf Coast, including parts of Mississippi, Alabama and Florida.
paras.zh: 截至周三上午，“伊萨亚斯”号距离墨西哥普罗格雷索海岸约 260 英里（420 公里），美国国家海洋和大气管理局 (NOAA) 预测，它正朝着美国墨西哥湾沿岸前进，包括密西西比州、阿拉巴马州和佛罗里达州的部分地区。

paras.en: Isaias’s winds are up to some 45 miles per hour (75 kilometers per hour) as of this writing. To be considered a hurricane, winds must hit or surpass 74 mph (119 kmh).
paras.zh: 截至撰写本文时，伊萨亚斯的风速高达每小时 45 英里（75 公里）。风速必须达到或超过 74 英里/小时（119 公里/小时）才能被视为飓风。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: If Isaias makes landfall as expected, the storm will likely bring strong gusts and heavy rainfall, with the potential for flash flooding and dangerous storm surge, says Jennifer Tate, a meteorologist at NOAA’s Weather Prediction Center.
paras.zh: 美国国家海洋和大气管理局天气预报中心的气象学家詹妮弗·泰特表示，如果伊萨亚斯如期登陆，这场风暴可能会带来强阵风和强降雨，并可能引发山洪和危险的风暴潮。

paras.en: As Scientific American previously reported, hurricane activity in the Atlantic typically begins in June and peaks in September. But this year the region has been quiet—with no hurricanes all season. Soon-to-be Hurricane Isaias would mark a historically late arrival for the first hurricane of the season.
paras.zh: 正如《科学美国人》之前报道的那样，大西洋的飓风活动通常在六月开始，在九月达到高峰。但今年该地区一直很安静——整个季节都没有飓风。即将到来的飓风伊萨亚斯将标志着本季度首场飓风的到来历史性地较晚。

paras.en: The quiet is in part linked to El Niño, meteorologists say. In an El Niño year, waters in the Pacific are unusually warm. This can drive global weather patterns, including in the Atlantic Ocean. There high vertical wind shear—changes in wind speed or direction with altitude—typically make it difficult for hurricanes to form during El Niño years.
paras.zh: 气象学家说，这种安静在一定程度上与厄尔尼诺现象有关。在厄尔尼诺年，太平洋海水异常温暖。这可以驱动全球天气模式，包括大西洋。垂直风切变（风速或风向随高度的变化而变化）通常会使厄尔尼诺年飓风难以形成。

paras.en: “It is common during El Niño patterns for the Atlantic to be quieter in terms of hurricanes,” Tate says, “whereas the eastern Pacific, and the Pacific in general, is more active. And we have seen that this year.”
paras.zh: 泰特说：“在厄尔尼诺现象期间，大西洋的飓风较为平静，这是很常见的，而东太平洋和整个太平洋则更加活跃。今年我们已经看到了这一点。”

paras.en: Indeed, in the Pacific, hurricanes have threatened Hawaii to an unusually high degree this season.
paras.zh: 事实上，在太平洋地区，本季节飓风对夏威夷的威胁达到了异常严重的程度。

paras.en: For those on the Gulf Coast, Tate recommends staying up to date on hurricane forecasts, getting prepared with food and supplies in the case of a power outage and following any local evacuation orders.
paras.zh: 对于墨西哥湾沿岸的人们，泰特建议及时了解最新的飓风预报，准备好食物和补给以防停电，并遵守当地的疏散命令。

articles.title: Here’s how brain-eating amoebas may infect people
articles.author: Meghan Rosen

paras.en: Some deadly amoebas may be primed to invade the brain.
paras.zh: 一些致命的阿米巴原虫可能准备好入侵大脑。

paras.en: Naegleria fowleri, known widely as the brain-eating amoeba, typically dine on bacteria in ponds. But the amoeba’s meal-seeking skills might make it uniquely suited to crawling up people’s noses and into their brains.
paras.zh: 福氏耐格里阿米巴原虫被广泛称为食脑变形虫，通常以池塘中的细菌为食。但阿米巴原虫的寻食能力可能使其特别适合爬上人们的鼻子并进入他们的大脑。

paras.en: Naegleria amoebas are intrepid explorers, probing nooks and crannies in the lab — and they’re persistent, too. When creeping down narrow passageways, the amoebas charge relentlessly forward, almost never turning back, researchers report September 10 in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. “They’re like robots,” says Lillian Fritz-Laylin, a cell biologist at the University of Massachusetts Amherst. “They just go and go and go.”
paras.zh: 变形虫耐格里阿米巴是勇敢的探索者，探索实验室的角落和缝隙——而且它们也很顽强。研究人员于 9 月 10 日在《美国国家科学院院刊》上报道称，当阿米巴原虫爬过狭窄的通道时，它们会毫不留情地向前冲锋，几乎从不回头。 “它们就像机器人，”马萨诸塞大学阿默斯特分校的细胞生物学家莉莲·弗里茨·雷林说。 “他们只是走啊走啊。”

paras.en: Such persistence might help these tiny, single-celled creatures make the marathon journey from the nostrils all the way to the brain. Fritz-Laylin’s work helps flesh out a largely skeletal picture of Naegleria behavior. “We know almost nothing about the basic biology of these organisms,” she says.
paras.zh: 这种坚持可能会帮助这些微小的单细胞生物完成从鼻孔一直到大脑的马拉松旅程。弗里茨·雷林的工作有助于充实耐格氏耐格里虫行为的基本框架。 “我们对这些生物体的基本生物学几乎一无所知，”她说。

paras.en: N. fowleri amoebas don’t routinely harm humans. They usually dwell in warm bodies of fresh water, where they squirm through sediment and mind their own business. But on rare occasions, the creatures can be washed up a swimmer’s nose. As the amoebas migrate through the nasal cavity and into the brain, they destroy and eat tissue. Then they begin to reproduce, usually with lethal consequences. The United States typically sees fewer than 10 Naegleria infections each year, often at summer swimming spots, but nearly every one is fatal.
paras.zh: 福氏阿米巴原虫通常不会伤害人类。它们通常居住在温暖的淡水中，在沉积物中蠕动并专注于自己的事情。但在极少数情况下，这些生物可能会被游泳者的鼻子冲走。当变形虫通过鼻腔迁移到大脑时，它们会破坏并吞噬组织。然后它们开始繁殖，通常会带来致命的后果。美国每年通常出现不到 10 例耐格里虫感染，通常发生在夏季游泳场所，但几乎每一种都是致命的。

paras.en: In the lab, Fritz-Laylin’s team tested Naegleria amoebas’ ability to move through different environments. They focused on N. gruberi, a harmless species that shares behaviors with its brain-eating relative. “It’s a lot safer to work with something that can’t kill you,” Fritz-Laylin says.
paras.zh: 在实验室中，Fritz-Laylin 的团队测试了变形虫耐格里阿米巴在不同环境中移动的能力。他们关注的是格鲁伯氏猪笼草，这是一种无害的物种，其行为与其食脑亲戚有共同之处。 “与不会杀死你的东西一起工作要安全得多，”弗里茨·雷林说。

paras.en: The researchers placed the amoebas on glass-bottom dishes containing narrow microchannels and watched them move under a microscope. They squeezed through channels smaller than themselves and seemed to be interested in exploring. When the amoebas encountered a channel opening, they very rarely left it, Fritz-Laylin says. Confinement sometimes sped them up, too. Inside the largest channels tested, the amoebas still zipped along twice as fast as cells on the outside.
paras.zh: 研究人员将阿米巴原虫放在含有狭窄微通道的玻璃底培养皿上，并在显微镜下观察它们的移动。他们挤过比自己还小的通道，似乎有兴趣探索。弗里茨-雷林说，当变形虫遇到通道开口时，它们很少离开它。禁闭有时也会加快他们的速度。在测试的最大通道内，变形虫的移动速度仍然是外部细胞的两倍。

paras.en: Naegleria’s persistence and need for speed may make it unique. The team didn’t observe the same behaviors in a different type of amoeba tested. Such attributes probably make Naegleria well-adapted to hunting bacteria in pond sediments, says Fritz-Laylin, who is also a Howard Hughes Medical Institute investigator. But those innocent behaviors could also explain N. fowleri’s dark side. Put one at “the wrong place at the wrong time,” she says, “and it can cause devastating infection.”
paras.zh: 耐格里虫的坚持和对速度的需求可能使其独一无二。研究小组在测试的不同类型阿米巴原虫中没有观察到相同的行为。霍华德休斯医学研究所研究员弗里茨-莱林说，这些特性可能使耐格里氏耐格里虫非常适合捕猎池塘沉积物中的细菌。但这些无辜的行为也可以解释福氏猪笼草的阴暗面。她说，“在错误的时间、错误的地点，可能会导致毁灭性的感染。”

articles.title: Remember the ‘caregiving kills’ study? Reality is more nuanced
articles.author: Sujata Gupta

paras.en: When social and affective neuroscientist Naomi Eisenberger’s dad developed dementia, she knew the popular wisdom. Caring for him could shave years off her life. But Eisenberger, of UCLA, was skeptical. Caring for her dad, who died in January, was stressful but also meaningful, she says. “It gave me a lot of joy to bring him some happiness.”
paras.zh: 当社会和情感神经科学家内奥米·艾森伯格的父亲患上痴呆症时，她知道流行的智慧。照顾他可能会缩短她的寿命。但加州大学洛杉矶分校的艾森伯格对此表示怀疑。她说，照顾一月份去世的父亲很有压力，但也很有意义。 “给他带来一些快乐让我感到非常高兴。”

paras.en: Caregiving kills as an idea first emerged in the scientific literature almost three decades ago. Distressed caregivers were 63 percent more likely to die within four years than non-caregivers, psychiatrists Richard Schulz and Scott Beach reported in 1999 in the Journal of the American Medical Association. The finding has since been cited almost 5,300 times, including almost 300 times in the past two years.
paras.zh: 大约三十年前，“看护致死”这一概念首次出现在科学文献中。 1999 年，精神病学家理查德·舒尔茨 (Richard Schulz) 和斯科特·比奇 (Scott Beach) 在《美国医学会杂志》上发表报告称，陷入困境的看护者四年内死亡的可能性比非看护者高出 63%。此后，这一发现被引用了近 5,300 次，其中过去两年被引用了近 300 次。

paras.en: But researchers have largely failed to replicate that finding, with considerable research showing instead that caregiving links with living longer, Eisenberger and colleagues report in September in Biopsychosocial Science and Medicine. Caregiving stress may be softened by humans’ hardwired propensity to help others in need, the researchers suspect.
paras.zh: 但研究人员在很大程度上未能复制这一发现，大量研究表明护理与寿命延长有关，艾森伯格及其同事在 9 月份的《生物心理社会科学与医学》杂志上报告说。研究人员怀疑，人类天生就有帮助有需要的人的倾向，这可能会减轻照顾压力。

paras.en: Silence surrounding caregiving’s positives is probably well-intentioned. In 2025, almost one-quarter of all adults in the United States, some 63 million people, provided care to adults or children with a medical condition or disability, according to a 2025 report by AARP and the National Alliance for Caregiving. Almost 65 percent of caregivers surveyed reported experiencing moderate or high emotional stress and almost half reported financial difficulties. Yet financial and emotional support for caregivers remains limited, the report notes.
paras.zh: 对护理的积极作用保持沉默可能是善意的。根据 AARP 和国家护理联盟 2025 年的一份报告，到 2025 年，美国近四分之一的成年人（约 6300 万人）为患有疾病或残疾的成年人或儿童提供护理。近 65% 的受访护理人员表示面临中度或高度情绪压力，近一半的护理人员表示经济困难。然而报告指出，对护理人员的经济和情感支持仍然有限。

paras.en: Highlighting caregiving’s pros could jeopardize what little help is available, says sociologist and gerontologist Rebecca Utz of the University of Utah in Salt Lake City. “I don’t like to take our foot off the pedal and say that caregiving is so positive because it’s hard, and people need support.”
paras.zh: 盐湖城犹他大学的社会学家和老年学家丽贝卡·乌茨 (Rebecca Utz) 表示，强调看护的优点可能会危及现有的有限帮助。 “我不想把我们的脚从踏板上移开，说护理是如此积极，因为它很困难，人们需要支持。”

paras.en: But painting caregiving as wholly negative, rather than nuanced, erases insight into how caregiving might also protect health, Eisenberger and colleagues argue. Most stressors, such as work-related burnout, link with chronic inflammation. Caregiving is less likely to show that link. Understanding that caregiving paradox could reveal how the body can withstand stress, Eisenberger says.
paras.zh: 但艾森伯格和同事认为，将护理描述为完全消极的而非细致入微的，会抹杀护理如何保护健康的见解。大多数压力源，例如与工作相关的倦怠，都与慢性炎症有关。护理不太可能显示出这种联系。艾森伯格说，了解护理悖论可以揭示身体如何承受压力。

paras.en: Moreover, helping a loved one may bring unexpected benefits, Eisenberger says. She cites a 2003 study in The Gerontologist showing that adult children who did not care for a parent with severe disabilities experienced more depression than those who did, though the researchers could not show causation. “I’m not suggesting everyone go out and engage in informal caregiving,” Eisenberger says. “I’m trying to make informal caregiving [feel] a little less scary.”
paras.zh: 此外，艾森伯格说，帮助亲人可能会带来意想不到的好处。她引用了《老年学家》2003 年的一项研究，该研究表明，不照顾父母患有严重残疾的成年子女比那些照顾父母的成年子女更容易患抑郁症，尽管研究人员无法证明其中的因果关系。 “我并不是建议每个人都出去从事非正式护理，”艾森伯格说。 “我正在努力让非正式护理[感觉]不那么可怕。”

paras.en: Caregiving was labeled as life-threatening
paras.zh: 护理被标记为危及生命

paras.en: In highlighting the need for researchers to take caregiver well-being seriously, the 1999 study was groundbreaking, Eisenberger and colleagues write. But it had design flaws.
paras.zh: 艾森伯格及其同事写道，1999 年的研究具有开创性，强调了研究人员认真对待护理人员福祉的必要性。但它存在设计缺陷。

paras.en: Schulz and Beach, both of the University of Pittsburgh, compared mortality rates across a four-year period from over 800 individuals. Roughly half the participants had disabled spouses, with some serving as caregivers and others not; the other half had nondisabled spouses and served as the control. Caregiving spouses filled out self-reports indicating their degree of mental strain.
paras.zh: 匹兹堡大学的舒尔茨和比奇比较了 800 多人在四年内的死亡率。大约一半的参与者有残疾配偶，其中一些人担任照顾者，另一些人则不然；另一半的配偶没有残疾，作为对照组。照顾配偶的配偶填写自我报告，表明他们的精神紧张程度。

paras.en: Over the next four years, 103 participants died. Schulz and Beach zoomed in on mortality rates among one subgroup — spousal caregivers reporting considerable strain. Of those distressed caregivers, 17 percent died during the study period compared with 9 percent of control group members.
paras.zh: 在接下来的四年里，103 名参与者死亡。舒尔茨和比奇重点研究了一个亚群体的死亡率——配偶照顾者报告称压力相当大。在那些陷入困境的护理人员中，有 17% 的人在研究期间死亡，而对照组成员的这一比例为 9%。

paras.en: But buried in the data was another finding, Eisenberger and colleagues note: Individuals not providing care to their disabled spouses still died at the same rate as caregivers experiencing distress. Individuals with sick and healthy spouses occupy different realities, largely invalidating comparisons between those groups, Eisenberger says. In this case, the findings suggest that having a sick or disabled spouse, and not caregiving status, increases one’s likelihood of dying.
paras.zh: 但艾森伯格和同事指出，数据中隐藏着另一个发现：不向残疾配偶提供护理的个人的死亡率仍然与经历痛苦的​​护理人员的死亡率相同。艾森伯格说，配偶患病和健康的人面临着不同的现实，这在很大程度上使这些群体之间的比较无效。在这种情况下，研究结果表明，配偶生病或残疾，而不是照顾状态，会增加一个人的死亡可能性。

paras.en: More than 6,000 caregivers were asked to evaluate both the sense of purpose and emotional stress associated with caregiving. Their answers illustrate the role’s emotional duality.
paras.zh: 超过 6,000 名护理人员被要求评估与护理相关的使命感和情绪压力。他们的回答说明了这个角色的情感二元性。

paras.en: The team is not the first to dispute the idea that caregiving kills. That list includes Schulz himself, who coauthored a 2009 Psychological Science study titled, “Caregiving behavior is associated with decreased mortality risk.” (Neither Schulz nor Beach could be reached for comment.) That study, though, has been cited less than 400 times, with just a couple dozen citations in the past two years.
paras.zh: 该团队并不是第一个对护理致死这一观点提出质疑的团队。该名单中包括舒尔茨本人，他在 2009 年与人合着了一项心理科学研究，题为“看护行为与降低死亡风险相关”。 （无法联系到舒尔茨和比奇发表评论。）不过，该研究被引用的次数不到 400 次，在过去两年中仅被引用了几十次。

paras.en: “I … assumed that the field would have taken notice,” says evolutionary and social psychologist Stephanie Brown, an author on the 2009 paper and a similar 2014 review of caregiving in Social Issues and Policy Review. But “slam pieces on caregiving” remain on prominent display in doctor’s offices and other medical settings, says Brown, of the Renaissance School of Medicine at Stony Brook University in New York.
paras.zh: “我……以为这个领域会注意到，”进化和社会心理学家斯蒂芬妮·布朗（Stephanie Brown）说，她是 2009 年这篇论文的作者，也是《社会问题和政策评论》2014 年类似的护理评论的作者。但纽约石溪大学文艺复兴医学院的布朗表示，“有关护理的大肆宣传”仍然在医生办公室和其他医疗场所的显着位置展示。

paras.en: Caregivers are stressed. Biology may help compensate
paras.zh: 照顾者压力很大。生物学可能有助于补偿

paras.en: More recent research hints at why caregiving, a tremendously stressful undertaking, may not kill.
paras.zh: 最近的研究暗示了为什么看护这种压力巨大的工作可能不会致命。

paras.en: It’s increasingly accepted that stress can trigger systemic inflammation that then compromises the immune system. In theory, stressed caregivers should be inflamed. They’re not, researchers reported in 2020 in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. That study relied on data from more than 30,000 U.S. adults. In surveys taken in the early 2000s and the 2010s, participants indicated their caregiver status, type and intensity of care being given, and experiences of strain. They also provided blood samples.
paras.zh: 人们越来越认识到，压力会引发全身炎症，进而损害免疫系统。从理论上讲，承受压力的看护者应该会发炎。研究人员在 2020 年《美国国家科学院院刊》上报道称，事实并非如此。该研究依赖于 30,000 多名美国成年人的数据。在 2000 年代初期和 2010 年代进行的调查中，参与者表明了他们的护理人员状况、护理类型和强度以及紧张经历。他们还提供了血液样本。

paras.en: The scientists zoomed in on roughly 250 people who became regular caregivers and analyzed their blood samples for six inflammation-related biomarkers. Those biomarkers did not go up, on average, when people transitioned to caregiving, the team found. Nor did they go up relative to a matched control group of non-caregivers selected from the larger sample. Those findings held true for even the most stressed caregivers, including spouses caring for a partner with dementia.
paras.zh: 科学家们重点关注了大约 250 名成为定期护理人员的人，并分析了他们的血液样本中的 6 种与炎症相关的生物标志物。研究小组发现，当人们转向护理时，这些生物标记物平均并没有上升。相对于从较大样本中选出的非照顾者的匹配对照组，它们也没有上升。即使是压力最大的护理人员，包括照顾患有痴呆症的伴侣的配偶，这些发现也适用。

paras.en: How, though, are caregivers largely avoiding inflammation associated with chronic stress? “We don’t really know,” says gerontologist and clinical psychologist William Haley of the University of South Florida in Tampa. “There’s a lot of mysteries here.”
paras.zh: 然而，护理人员如何在很大程度上避免与慢性压力相关的炎症呢？ “我们真的不知道，”坦帕南佛罗里达大学的老年学家和临床心理学家威廉·黑利说。 “这里有很多谜团。”

paras.en: Eisenberger and colleagues theorize that the key to the caregiving paradox may lie in a biological system that evolved among mammals to protect offspring that remain helpless well after birth. That “mammalian caregiving system” seems to encourage caring and tamp down the normal stress response that tells people to flee danger, at least when their baby is involved, Eisenberger says.
paras.zh: 艾森伯格及其同事推测，照顾悖论的关键可能在于哺乳动物进化出的生物系统，以保护出生后仍无助的后代。艾森伯格说，这种“哺乳动物照顾系统”似乎鼓励照顾并抑制正常的压力反应，这种压力反应告诉人们要逃离危险，至少在涉及婴儿时是这样。

paras.en: Studies primarily in rodents hint at how that caregiving system works, Eisenberger notes. And emerging evidence in humans suggests that this system kicks on even in non-parenting contexts, such as holding onto a partner in pain or giving money to family. In preliminary work, Brown and colleagues even saw signs of it among strangers who bonded during an activity.
paras.zh: 艾森伯格指出，主要针对啮齿类动物的研究揭示了这一护理系统的运作方式。人类身上不断出现的证据表明，即使在非养育子女的情况下，这个系统也会发挥作用，比如在痛苦中抓住伴侣或给家人钱。在初步工作中，布朗和同事甚至在活动期间结识的陌生人中发现了这种迹象。

paras.en: Researchers are missing fascinating questions
paras.zh: 研究人员错过了一些有趣的问题

paras.en: The contradictory feelings Eisenberger experienced while caring for her dad are common. Caregivers can’t disentangle the advantages of the mammalian caregiving system from the strain of helping. Yet over half of caregivers surveyed by AARP reported that caring for a loved one gave them a sense of purpose.
paras.zh: 艾森伯格在照顾父亲时经历的矛盾感受很常见。护理人员无法将哺乳动物护理系统的优势与帮助的压力区分开来。然而，美国退休人员协会 (AARP) 调查显示，超过一半的护理人员表示，照顾亲人给了他们一种使命感。

paras.en: Ironically, minimizing potential positives to protect caregivers may do more harm than good, researchers say. Caregivers may hear only how awful their next several months or years may be. Others might run from the responsibility and later experience regret.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，讽刺的是，为了保护护理人员而最大限度地减少潜在的积极因素可能弊大于利。护理人员可能只会听到他们接下来的几个月或几年可能会多么糟糕。其他人可能会逃避责任，然后后悔。

paras.en: “What if we tell people that … helping others can be really fulfilling even if it can be stressful, too?” Eisenberger says.
paras.zh: “如果我们告诉人们......帮助他人可以真正让人感到满足，即使它也可能有压力呢？”艾森伯格说。

paras.en: Reticence around caregiving’s benefits has also hampered scientists’ ability to advise people undertaking such a difficult role, Eisenberger and colleagues note. Can feeling compassion for a sick loved one turn on the mammalian caregiving system, or does one have to provide care? What if someone has a fraught relationship with the sick family member? Ultimately, when does the stress of opting out of caregiving outweigh the stress of opting in? Framing caregiving as entirely negative means those questions rarely even get asked.
paras.zh: 艾森伯格和同事指出，对护理好处的沉默也阻碍了科学家为承担如此困难角色的人们提供建议的能力。对生病的亲人的同情可以开启哺乳动物的护理系统，还是必须提供护理？如果有人与生病的家庭成员关系紧张怎么办？最终，选择退出护理的压力何时超过选择接受护理的压力？将护理视为完全消极意味着这些问题很少被问到。

articles.title: A quake on Mars may have set these rocks rolling
articles.author: Katherine Kornei

paras.en: Earthquakes frequently trigger rock falls. Now there’s solid evidence marsquakes can send boulders tumbling, too.
paras.zh: 地震经常引发岩石坠落。现在有确凿的证据表明火星地震也会导致巨石翻滚。

paras.en: Scientists mined high-resolution imagery of the Red Planet taken shortly after a recent temblor and found hundreds of new imprints left by tumbling boulders, researchers report September 2 in npj Space Exploration. Such rockfalls can be used as a proxy for seismic data, which is difficult to collect across the solar system.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 9 月 2 日在 npj Space Exploration 上报告称，科学家们挖掘了最近一次地震后不久拍摄的这颗红色星球的高分辨率图像，发现了数百个翻滚巨石留下的新印记。这种落石可以用作地震数据的代理，而地震数据很难在整个太阳系中收集。

paras.en: The data were collected with NASA’s InSight lander, which touched down on Mars in 2018. Over the next four years, its seismometer detected more than a thousand marsquakes. Many of those temblors originated in a region known as Cerberus Fossae, just north of the Martian equator. That’s a dynamic landscape riddled with slopes, cracks and rocks on the move, says Vijayan, a planetary scientist at the Physical Research Laboratory in Ahmedabad, India, who goes by a single name. “Thousands and thousands of boulders have fallen.”
paras.zh: 这些数据是通过 NASA 的 InSight 着陆器收集的，该着陆器于 2018 年登陆火星。在接下来的四年里，其地震仪检测到了一千多次火星地震。许多地震起源于火星赤道以北的一个名为塞伯鲁斯窝的地区。印度艾哈迈达巴德物理研究实验室的行星科学家维贾扬（Vijayan）说，这是一个动态的景观，布满了斜坡、裂缝和移动的岩石。 “成千上万的巨石倒塌了。”

paras.en: Vijayan and his collaborators focused on one well-detected marsquake captured by InSight that occurred in July 2019 just a few tens of kilometers from Cerberus Fossae. By comparing images taken in June 2019 and December 2020, the researchers discovered 27 new linelike features. Each was composed of tens to hundreds of distinct marks. These structures were most likely tracks created by boulders bouncing downhill, the team concluded.
paras.zh: Vijayan 和他的合作者重点研究了 InSight 捕捉到的一场地震，该地震发生在 2019 年 7 月，距离 Cerberus Fossae 仅几十公里。通过比较 2019 年 6 月和 2020 年 12 月拍摄的图像，研究人员发现了 27 个新的线状特征。每个标记都由数十到数百个不同的标记组成。研究小组得出结论，这些结构很可能是巨石下坡时留下的痕迹。

paras.en: Using historical imagery, the researchers calculated that only about two such features form each year on average in Cerberus Fossae. “We have statistics of previous boulder falls,” says Bivas Das, a seismologist at the Physical Research Laboratory and a member of the research team. Recording 27 new structures over a span of just 18 months is wholly unexpected, Das says. “That’s a big increase.” The nearby marsquake recorded by InSight was probably the instigator, the team concluded.
paras.zh: 研究人员利用历史图像计算出，Cerberus Fossae 每年平均只有大约两个这样的特征。 “我们有以前巨石坠落的统计数据，”物理研究实验室的地震学家、研究小组成员比瓦斯·达斯（Bivas Das）说。 Das 表示，在短短 18 个月内记录了 27 个新结构，这完全出乎意料。 “这是一个很大的增长。”研究小组得出结论，洞察号记录的附近的火星地震可能是始作俑者。

paras.en: Mysteries remain, however. All of the rockfalls occurred on the north side of a prominent valley in Cerberus Fossae, despite more boulders being located on the south side of the valley. “That puzzles us,” Vijayan says. The complex landscape of Cerberus Fossae might well alter how seismic waves travel, making it difficult to predict how shaking will impact different areas, he says. “The wave propagation is going to be complicated.”
paras.zh: 然而，谜团依然存在。尽管更多的巨石位于山谷的南侧，但所有落石都发生在塞伯鲁斯窝沟的一个著名山谷的北侧。 “这让我们感到困惑，”维贾扬说。他说，Cerberus Fossae 的复杂景观很可能会改变地震波的传播方式，从而很难预测震动将如何影响不同地区。 “波的传播将会很复杂。”

paras.en: Looking for such boulder falls elsewhere could help space exploration efforts, the team suggests. Human settlements would do best avoiding areas that are seismically active, and tumbling boulders can be the proverbial canaries in the coal mine, Vijayan says. “They’re like a proxy in the absence of seismic data.”
paras.zh: 研究小组表示，在其他地方寻找此类巨石坠落可能有助于太空探索工作。维贾扬说，人类住区最好避开地震活跃的地区，而翻滚的巨石可能是煤矿里众所周知的金丝雀。 “在缺乏地震数据的情况下，它们就像一个代理。”

articles.title: A Hot Bath May Lower Your Blood Pressure More Than a 30-Minute Workout Can, Study Reveals
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: Taking a nice hot bath at the end of a long day is a wonderful way to unwind, but the end results can go way beyond simple relaxation.
paras.zh: 在漫长的一天结束后洗个热水澡是一种很好的放松方式，但最终的结果远远超出了简单的放松。

paras.en: In fact, the health benefits of sustained immersion in hot water can be truly surprising, and new research has just uncovered another remarkable effect of a good hot soak.
paras.zh: 事实上，持续浸泡在热水中对健康的好处确实令人惊讶，新的研究刚刚发现了良好的热水浸泡的另一个显着效果。

paras.en: In a study published in the European Journal of Applied Physiology, researchers found soaking in hot water for 30 minutes can trigger dramatic changes in the blood vessels beneath your skin, in some respects exceeding the effects produced by moderate exercise.
paras.zh: 在《欧洲应用生理学杂志》上发表的一项研究中，研究人员发现，在热水中浸泡 30 分钟可以引发皮肤下血管的巨大变化，在某些方面超过了适度运动所产生的效果。

paras.en: The hot water immersion even lowered people's blood pressure more than 30 minutes of moderate-intensity cycling.
paras.zh: 热水浸泡甚至可以降低中等强度骑行 30 分钟以上的血压。

paras.en: It's worth noting this was only a small experiment, and nobody's suggesting people should give up exercise to instead take more hot baths.
paras.zh: 值得注意的是，这只是一个小实验，没有人建议人们应该放弃锻炼而多洗热水澡。

paras.en: But for people who may be unable to exercise, hot water immersion, or other forms of what's known as passive heat therapy, may be an important way of getting some of the same health benefits that exercise can provide.
paras.zh: 但对于无法锻炼的人来说，热水浸泡或其他形式的被动热疗法可能是获得与锻炼相同的健康益处的重要方法。

paras.en: "Exercise training is a well-established stimulus for improving vascular health, in part by enhancing endothelial function, arterial compliance, and microvascular responsiveness," researchers explain in a new paper, led by first author and exercise physiologist Kristanti Wigati from the University of Western Australia.
paras.zh: 研究人员在一篇由第一作者、西澳大利亚大学运动生理学家 Kristanti Wigati 领导的新论文中解释道：“运动训练是改善血管健康的一种公认的刺激措施，部分是通过增强内皮功能、动脉顺应性和微血管反应性。”

paras.en: "However, recent global estimates indicate that approximately 31 percent of adults worldwide do not meet physical activity guidelines, supporting the need to explore adjunct or alternative interventions for individuals who may struggle with regular exercise participation."
paras.zh: “然而，最近的全球估计表明，全世界大约 31% 的成年人不符合体育活动指南，这表明有必要为那些可能难以定期参与锻炼的个人探索辅助或替代干预措施。”

paras.en: Hot water immersion, like exercise itself, provides an increase in blood flow and shear stress along the inside walls of blood vessels, which triggers adaptations that improve vascular function.
paras.zh: 与运动本身一样，热水浸泡会增加血管内壁的血流量和剪切应力，从而引发改善血管功能的适应。

paras.en: Previous research in young healthy adults has shown that repeated hot water immersion can improve blood vessel function, reduce arterial stiffness, and help blood vessels widen through nitric oxide.
paras.zh: 此前针对年轻健康成年人的研究表明，反复热水浸泡可以改善血管功能，降低动脉僵硬度，并通过一氧化氮帮助血管扩张。

paras.en: "These findings suggest that hot water immersion may act as an 'exercise-like' vascular stimulus, but evidence in older individuals with risk factors for cardiovascular disease who are unable to engage in conventional exercise is lacking," the researchers note.
paras.zh: 研究人员指出：“这些研究结果表明，热水浸泡可能起到‘类似运动’的血管刺激作用，但缺乏针对患有心血管疾病危险因素且无法进行常规运动的老年人的证据。”

paras.en: To plug the gap, the researchers recruited 25 adults aged 45–70 with overweight or obesity, with an average age of 59.
paras.zh: 为了填补这一空白，研究人员招募了 25 名年龄在 45-70 岁之间超重或肥胖的成年人，平均年龄为 59 岁。

paras.en: During the experiment, each of the participants completed two different interventions, in a random order, and separated by at least 72 hours.
paras.zh: 实验期间，每位参与者以随机顺序完成两次不同的干预措施，且间隔至少 72 小时。

paras.en: In one intervention, participants sat chest-deep for 30 minutes in hot water, which was maintained at a temperature of 40 °C (104 °F).
paras.zh: 在一项干预措施中，参与者坐在齐胸深的热水中 30 分钟，热水温度保持在 40 °C (104 °F)。

paras.en: In the other intervention, participants performed a moderate-intensity exercise session, cycling for 30 minutes on a stationary exercise bicycle, with the intensity corresponding to 60–70 percent of their maximum heart rate.
paras.zh: 在另一项干预措施中，参与者进行了中等强度的锻炼，即骑固定健身自行车 30 分钟，强度相当于最大心率的 60-70%。

paras.en: The participants had their heart rate, mean arterial pressure, and core body temperature monitored during the tests, and researchers also assessed tiny blood vessels in the participants' skin, using a non-invasive technique called optical coherence tomography (OCT).
paras.zh: 在测试过程中，参与者的心率、平均动脉压和核心体温受到监测，研究人员还使用一种称为光学相干断层扫描（OCT）的非侵入性技术评估了参与者皮肤中的微小血管。

paras.en: Results showed that, compared to the exercise intervention, the hot water immersion produced significantly larger increases in blood vessel diameter, blood flow, and blood velocity, as well as the density of microvessels with detectable blood flow.
paras.zh: 结果显示，与运动干预相比，热水浸泡使血管直径、血流量、血速度以及可检测到血流量的微血管密度显着增加。

paras.en: An indication of this can be seen in an OCT-derived image from participants' forearms, which visibly shows increased blood flow activity in the microvascular network after hot water immersion.
paras.zh: 从参与者前臂的 OCT 图像中可以看出这一点，该图像明显显示热水浸泡后微血管网络中的血流活动增加。

paras.en: "These pronounced microvascular responses were accompanied by a larger elevation in core body temperature and greater reductions in systolic and diastolic blood pressure following hot water immersion, whereas moderate-intensity exercise elicited a higher heart rate response," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“这些明显的微血管反应伴随着热水浸泡后核心体温的更大升高以及收缩压和舒张压的更大降低，而中等强度的运动会引发更高的心率反应。”

paras.en: "Collectively, these findings suggest that the larger microvascular responses observed after hot water immersion likely reflect the combined effects of direct local skin heating and greater systemic thermal strain imposed by passive heating."
paras.zh: “总的来说，这些发现表明，热水浸泡后观察到的更大的微血管反应可能反映了直接局部皮肤加热和被动加热施加的更大的全身热应变的综合影响。”

paras.en: The researchers say that hot water immersion promotes the widening of blood vessels, a process called vasodilation, which facilitates heat dissipation by redistributing blood flow to the skin.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，热水浸泡会促进血管扩张，这一过程称为血管舒张，通过重新分配皮肤的血流来促进热量散发。

paras.en: While the findings suggest hot water immersion could potentially hold promise as a complementary way of providing a vascular stimulus, the researchers are careful to point out there's much we still don't know.
paras.zh: 虽然研究结果表明热水浸泡可能有望作为提供血管刺激的补充方式，但研究人员小心地指出，我们仍然不知道很多。

paras.en: That's especially so since the experiment here was matched for time (30 minutes for each intervention), but not for the levels of thermal strain experienced by the body.
paras.zh: 尤其如此，因为这里的实验与时间匹配（每次干预 30 分钟），但与身体经历的热应变水平不匹配。

paras.en: "Accordingly, the present findings should not be interpreted as indicating that hot water immersion is intrinsically superior to moderate-intensity exercise per se; rather, they reflect the greater thermal strain achieved during hot water immersion, which elicited substantial shear-mediated vascular stimuli in the absence of active muscle contraction," the authors explain.
paras.zh: “因此，目前的研究结果不应被解释为表明热水浸泡本质上优于中等强度运动本身；相反，它们反映了热水浸泡期间实现的更大的热应变，这在没有主动肌肉收缩的情况下引发了大量剪切介导的血管刺激，”作者解释道。

paras.en: "This may be particularly relevant for clinical populations who are unable to engage in regular exercise, suggesting that hot water immersion could serve as a complementary or alternative strategy to induce beneficial vascular stimuli."
paras.zh: “这可能与无法进行定期锻炼的临床人群特别相关，表明热水浸泡可以作为诱导有益血管刺激的补充或替代策略。”

paras.en: The findings are reported in the European Journal of Applied Physiology.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《欧洲应用生理学杂志》上。

articles.title: Sexually Transmitted Diarrhea Is Exploding in The US. And It's Growing Resistant to Medicine
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: A gut pathogen that causes diarrhea and vomiting is morphing into a dangerous and difficult-to-treat sexually transmitted infection (STI).
paras.zh: 一种引起腹泻和呕吐的肠道病原体正在演变成一种危险且难以治疗的性传播感染（STI）。

paras.en: In the United States, roughly 450,000 people acquire shigellosis each year, which can lead to dysentery.
paras.zh: 在美国，每年大约有 45 万人感染志贺氏菌病，这可能导致痢疾。

paras.en: Historically, this highly contagious bug has mostly been spread through contaminated food or water during travel, and among young children in day care.
paras.zh: 从历史上看，这种高度传染性的细菌主要是在旅行期间通过受污染的食物或水以及在日托中心的幼儿中传播的。

paras.en: But since the turn of the century or so, Shigella bacteria have emerged as a sexually transmitted infection as well.
paras.zh: 但自本世纪之交左右以来，志贺氏菌也已成为一种性传播感染。

paras.en: Shigella infections can make anyone sick, but they are now considered 'endemic' in some communities of gay, bisexual and other men who have sex with men (GBMSM).
paras.zh: 志贺氏菌感染可以使任何人生病，但在一些同性恋、双性恋和其他男男性行为者 (GBMSM) 社区中，志贺氏菌感染现在被认为是“流行病”。

paras.en: Several of the strains transmitted in these communities have grown resistant to multiple antibiotics.
paras.zh: 在这些社区传播的一些菌株已经对多种抗生素产生了耐药性。

paras.en: Some are now superbugs, on the brink of becoming untreatable.
paras.zh: 有些现在已经成为超级细菌，处于无法治疗的边缘。

paras.en: A recent analysis from the US CDC found that among nearly 17,000 Shigella isolates, versions that were extensively drug-resistant (XDR) rose from 2011 to 2023.
paras.zh: 美国疾病预防控制中心 (CDC) 最近的一项分析发现，在近 17,000 种志贺氏菌分离株中，从 2011 年到 2023 年，广泛耐药 (XDR) 的菌株有所增加。

paras.en: In 2011, isolates that were resistant to five commonly used antibiotics made up 0 percent of the samples. By 2023, they made up 8.5 percent.
paras.zh: 2011 年，对五种常用抗生素具有耐药性的菌株占样本的 0%。到 2023 年，这一比例将达到 8.5%。

paras.en: The vast majority of these drug-resistant versions had infected adult men, many of whom had not traveled internationally in recent months.
paras.zh: 这些耐药病毒绝大多数感染了成年男性，其中许多人最近几个月没有出国旅行。

paras.en: Molecular biologist Shangxin Yang says hospital workers at the University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA) are now seeing roughly one case of extensively drug-resistant Shigella a month.
paras.zh: 分子生物学家杨尚欣表示，加州大学洛杉矶分校 (UCLA) 的医院工作人员现在每月大约会发现一例广泛耐药志贺氏菌。

paras.en: In 2022, by comparison, they saw just one case all year.
paras.zh: 相比之下，2022 年他们全年只看到一例。

paras.en: "It's almost like an explosion of this pathogen in the community," Yang told CIDRAP News at the University of Minnesota.
paras.zh: 杨在明尼苏达大学告诉 CIDRAP 新闻：“这几乎就像这种病原体在社区中爆发一样。”

paras.en: Sexually transmissible shigellosis was first reported in 1974, but it represented a minority of cases at the time.
paras.zh: 性传播志贺氏菌病首次报道于 1974 年，但当时仅占少数病例。

paras.en: Now, emerging evidence suggests that sexual contact is a major route of transmission.
paras.zh: 现在，新的证据表明性接触是主要的传播途径。

paras.en: It's difficult to verify this information, however, as patients and clinicians may not realize that Shigella can be sexually transmitted, and sexual history may not be recorded.
paras.zh: 然而，很难验证这一信息，因为患者和临床医生可能没有意识到志贺氏菌可以通过性传播，并且可能不会记录性史。

paras.en: That said, according to US CDC data, more than a third of patients with extensively drug-resistant shigellosis were hospitalized, and nearly half of those with known HIV status had HIV.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，根据美国疾病预防控制中心的数据，超过三分之一的广泛耐药志贺氏菌病患者住院治疗，而已知艾滋病毒感染状况的患者中近一半患有艾滋病毒。

paras.en: "Together, it's a very concerning pattern of XDR Shigella strains that are being seen among vulnerable populations," epidemiologist Naeemah Logan from the CDC told CIDRAP News.
paras.zh: 疾病预防控制中心的流行病学家 Naeemah Logan 告诉 CIDRAP 新闻：“总而言之，在弱势人群中发现了一种非常令人担忧的 XDR 志贺氏菌菌株模式。”

paras.en: "This is by no means unique to the US, but really part of a broader global pattern."
paras.zh: “这绝不是美国独有的，而是更广泛的全球格局的一部分。”

paras.en: Geneticist Kate Baker from the University of Cambridge, senior author of a recent study in The Lancet Infectious Diseases, has identified a similar surge in the United Kingdom.
paras.zh: 剑桥大学的遗传学家凯特·贝克（Kate Baker）是《柳叶刀传染病》最近一项研究的资深作者，她发现英国也出现了类似的激增。

paras.en: "Many men who have sex with men are unaware of the serious and increasing risk posed by sexually transmitted Shigella," said Baker in a July press release.
paras.zh: 贝克在 7 月份的新闻稿中表示：“许多男男性行为者并没有意识到性传播志贺氏菌带来的严重且日益增加的风险。”

paras.en: "This disease has gone from being relatively treatable with off-the-shelf drugs to being close to untreatable over the course of the last decade or so."
paras.zh: “在过去十年左右的时间里，这种疾病已经从相对可以用现成药物治疗到几乎无法治疗。”

paras.en: In March, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) warned that while most cases of Shigella resolve without treatment, more severe cases do require treatment, and "the options available are becoming limited."
paras.zh: 三月份，英国健康安全局 (UKHSA) 警告说，虽然大多数志贺氏菌病例无需治疗即可痊愈，但更严重的病例确实需要治疗，而且“可用的选择越来越有限”。

paras.en: In 2025, 86 percent of Shigella sonnei samples and 94 percent of Shigella flexneri samples tested by UKHSA researchers showed resistance to antibiotics.
paras.zh: 2025 年，UKHSA 研究人员测试的 86% 宋内志贺菌样本和 94% 福氏志贺菌样本显示出对抗生素的耐药性。

paras.en: These are the two most commonly spread strains through sexual contact among GBMSM in England.
paras.zh: 这是英格兰 GBMSM 中最常通过性接触传播的两种病毒。

paras.en: In previous research by Baker and others, up to a third of patients with sexually transmitted Shigella were hospitalized for an average of four to five days.
paras.zh: 在贝克等人之前的研究中，多达三分之一的性传播志贺氏菌患者平均住院四到五天。

paras.en: "This isn't just one form of sexually transmissible diarrhea," says Baker.
paras.zh: “这不仅仅是性传播腹泻的一种形式，”贝克说。

paras.en: "This is multiple overlapping variants emerging that are all quickly becoming resistant to the drugs we use to treat them. It's highly likely that if you contracted your Shigella through sex, you require different treatment to someone who contracted it through travel."
paras.zh: “这是多种重叠的变异体的出现，它们很快就会对我们用来治疗它们的药物产生耐药性。如果你通过性行为感染了志贺氏菌，那么你很可能需要与通过旅行感染志贺氏菌的人不同的治疗方法。”

paras.en: No one knows why that is, but Baker's 2026 study points to 'bystander resistance' as one driver.
paras.zh: 没有人知道这是为什么，但贝克 2026 年的研究指出，作为一名司机，“旁观者的抵制”。

paras.en: This means that an antibiotic meant for one pathogen may not be the right drug or dose for another present pathogen, thereby breeding resistance as a side effect.
paras.zh: 这意味着针对一种病原体的抗生素可能不是另一种现有病原体的正确药物或剂量，从而产生耐药性作为副作用。

paras.en: In response to the recent study, Alicia Calvo-Villamañán, a researcher at the Gulbenkian Institute for Molecular Medicine in Lisbon, Portugal, pointed out an intriguing association.
paras.zh: 针对最近的研究，葡萄牙里斯本古尔本基安分子医学研究所的研究员 Alicia Calvo-Villamañán 指出了一个有趣的关联。

paras.en: "When the UK's national treatment guidelines stopped recommending the use of [azithromycin] to treat gonorrhea infections," they wrote, "the emergence of azithromycin resistance in Shigella slowed down."
paras.zh: “当英国国家治疗指南停止推荐使用[阿奇霉素]治疗淋病感染时，”他们写道，“志贺菌对阿奇霉素耐药性的出现减缓了。”

paras.en: That doesn't mean one is causing the other, but it suggests that treating other STIs may be a risk factor for drug-resistant Shigella infections, which aren't often screened as STIs.
paras.zh: 这并不意味着一种疾病会导致另一种疾病，但它表明治疗其他性传播感染可能是耐药志贺氏菌感染的一个危险因素，而这种感染通常不会被筛查为性传播感染。

paras.en: The California Department of Public Health says that the best way to prevent Shigella infection from sex is to not have sex with someone who has had diarrhea in the last two weeks.
paras.zh: 加州公共卫生部表示，预防性交感染志贺氏菌的最佳方法是不要与过去两周患有腹泻的人发生性关系。

paras.en: Using barriers during oral and anal sex is also advised, as is washing up before and after sex.
paras.zh: 还建议在口交和肛交期间使用屏障，以及在性交前后进行清洗。

paras.en: To minimize transmission, anyone who suspects they may have Shigella should get tested and seek treatment if necessary.
paras.zh: 为了最大限度地减少传播，任何怀疑自己可能感染志贺氏菌的人都应该接受检测，并在必要时寻求治疗。

paras.en: "Clinicians should be asking patients with dysentery about sexual transmission and giving advice accordingly," said Daniel Richardson, a consultant in sexual health at University Hospitals Sussex in July.
paras.zh: 苏塞克斯大学医院的性健康顾问丹尼尔·理查森 (Daniel Richardson) 7 月表示：“临床医生应该询问痢疾患者有关性传播的情况，并给出相应的建议。”

paras.en: "They need to know that sexually transmitted Shigella has more antimicrobial resistance than other forms of the disease, and that patients may need checking for other sexually transmissible illnesses."
paras.zh: “他们需要知道，性传播志贺氏菌比其他形式的疾病具有更强的抗菌耐药性，并且患者可能需要检查其他性传播疾病。”

articles.title: One Simple Habit May Give Your Bowels a Boost Within Minutes
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: Nobody likes the feeling of being constipated, but the consequences of being backed up might be more serious than you realize.
paras.zh: 没有人喜欢便秘的感觉，但便秘的后果可能比你想象的更严重。

paras.en: Research shows that the amount of time poop sticks around in your body can have an overlooked impact on your health and quality of life, with constipation being a known risk factor for cardiovascular events, including heart attacks, heart failure, and stroke, among other complications.
paras.zh: 研究表明，粪便在体内停留的时间可能会对您的健康和生活质量产生被忽视的影响，便秘是心血管事件的已知危险因素，包括心脏病发作、心力衰竭和中风等并发症。

paras.en: Fortunately, there are steps you can take to get things moving again, and one of the easiest strategies is simply doing some light exercise.
paras.zh: 幸运的是，您可以采取一些步骤来让事情重新开始，最简单的策略之一就是做一些轻微的运动。

paras.en: We know that people who do regular exercise have less risk of developing constipation, whereas low levels of physical activity and high amounts of sedentary behavior may increase your chances of getting blocked.
paras.zh: 我们知道，经常锻炼的人患便秘的风险较小，而低水平的体力活动和大量的久坐行为可能会增加便秘的风险。

paras.en: What's less clear, though, is what exercise actually does inside the body to help prevent or alleviate constipation, but a recent study published in Scientific Reports offers some plausible explanations – and suggests physical activity has an "immediate effect" on your gut, which could help ease the problem.
paras.zh: 然而，不太清楚的是，运动在体内到底能起到什么作用来帮助预防或缓解便秘，但最近发表在《科学报告》上的一项研究提供了一些合理的解释，并表明体力活动对肠道有“直接影响”，这可能有助于缓解问题。

paras.en: In an experiment, a team of researchers from Fujita Health University in Japan recruited 21 healthy adult participants specifically to listen to the sounds of their bowels.
paras.zh: 在一项实验中，日本藤田保健大学的一组研究人员招募了 21 名健康成年参与者，专门听他们肠子的声音。

paras.en: "Walking can serve as an effective, immediate tool for stimulating bowel function." – senior author and rehabilitation physician Yohei Otaka
paras.zh: “步行可以作为刺激肠道功能的有效、直接的工具。” – 资深作者、康复医师 Yohei Otaka

paras.en: Ordinarily, other people's bowel sounds aren't something you want to hear, but in terms of medical analysis, they're an established and non-invasive indicator of gut motility – the muscle movements that move food along the gastrointestinal (GI) tract during the digestion process.
paras.zh: 通常，您不想听到其他人的肠鸣音，但从医学分析的角度来看，它们是肠道蠕动的既定且非侵入性指标，即在消化过程中沿着胃肠 (GI) 道移动食物的肌肉运动。

paras.en: "Bowel sounds have been used as indirect measurements of gut motility since the early 1900s," the team explains in their paper, led by physical therapist Kento Katagiri.
paras.zh: “自 1900 年代初以来，肠鸣音一直被用来间接测量肠道蠕动，”物理治疗师 Kento Katagiri 领导的研究小组在论文中解释道。

paras.en: "The bowel sound is produced by the turbulence caused by gut motility during the movement of liquids and gases through the intestinal tract."
paras.zh: “肠鸣音是由液体和气体通过肠道时肠道蠕动引起的湍流产生的。”

paras.en: In the experiment, the participants rested for five minutes, then had their bowel sounds measured using an electronic stethoscope to establish what their baseline level of gut motility sounded like.
paras.zh: 在实验中，参与者休息五分钟，然后使用电子听诊器测量肠鸣音，以确定他们的肠道蠕动的基线水平。

paras.en: The stethoscope readings were taken at least two hours after eating, to minimize the effects of food intake during the experiment.
paras.zh: 听诊器读数在进食后至少两个小时进行，以尽量减少实验过程中食物摄入的影响。

paras.en: Next, participants walked on a treadmill at a comfortable walking speed for 20 minutes – approximately 3,000 steps, which in previous research was a level of walking shown to improve bowel clearance in patients preparing for a colonoscopy.
paras.zh: 接下来，参与者以舒适的步行速度在跑步机上行走 20 分钟（大约 3,000 步），在之前的研究中，该步行水平被证明可以改善准备结肠镜检查的患者的肠道清除率。

paras.en: After the treadmill, the participants again had their bowel sounds measured to see how the light exercise session might have affected their gut motility.
paras.zh: 跑步机结束后，参与者再次测量肠鸣音，以了解轻度运动对他们肠道蠕动的影响。

paras.en: When the scientists analyzed the recordings, they found that three separate bowel-sound measures increased for 1–2 minutes after the physical activity, including the sound index (SI – the overall strength and amplitude of the sounds) and the duration and number of bowel sounds.
paras.zh: 当科学家分析这些录音时，他们发现三个独立的肠鸣音测量在体力活动后 1-2 分钟内增加，包括声音指数（SI - 声音的整体强度和幅度）以及肠鸣音的持续时间和数量。

paras.en: According to the researchers, the increase in the bowel sounds may reflect changes in gut motility induced by the physical activity, and could be a result of increased peristaltic movement – wave-like muscular contractions that propel food through the GI tract.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，肠鸣音的增加可能反映了体力活动引起的肠道蠕动的变化，并且可能是蠕动运动增加的结果，即推动食物通过胃肠道的波状肌肉收缩。

paras.en: As for how exercise triggers this, the researchers suggest two possible mechanisms inside the body that might play a role.
paras.zh: 至于运动如何引发这种情况，研究人员提出了体内两种可能发挥作用的机制。

paras.en: Firstly, it's possible the effects seen could relate to changes in the autonomic nervous system during physical activity, with an increase in parasympathetic nervous system activity directly after exercise stimulating gut motility.
paras.zh: 首先，所观察到的影响可能与体力活动期间自主神经系统的变化有关，在运动刺激肠道蠕动后，副交感神经系统活动立即增加。
